bibl.author: P. Ovidius Naso
bibl.title: P. Ovidii Nasonis operum tomus primus
bibl.ref: Washington and Lee University Special Collections, PA6519 .A2 1751, volume 1
bibl.note: One-based viewer images 186–187; printed page numbers are 44 lower. Archive page labels differ from both. The actual images, rather than another witness or uncorrected OCR, supply the readings.

normalization.p: Source spelling, capitalization, punctuation, written ampersands and visible accents are retained. Long s and typographic ligatures are represented by standard s and constituent letters. Letter spacing in display capitals and quotation glyph shapes may be represented schematically. No modern-edition readings are substituted.

segmentation.p: Each l represents one canonical verse, with stable numbering and a link to its existing image region. Source verse order and headings are retained. Couplet grouping and canonical line numbers are editorial. A displaced word may remain within its verse with its position marked.

Both readers checked actual full-page line starts. The regular visible insets are retained, with an additional two-character approximation at verse 2 for the enlarged initial’s exceptional opening inset. This is source layout evidence, not a rule inferred from verse parity.

correction.p: Uncertain readings remain locally marked with unclear or gap. Observations and uncertainties are documented for a different source reader; ink colour alone does not establish erasure or a separate hand.

revisionDesc.change: First reader inspected and transcribed all 48 verses from the source images; independent source review pending.

Independent second source pass checked every extant verse, source heading, page furniture and full-page line starts; corrected supported readings and documented the source layout in W-3.10-second-pass.md.

Focused independent image reinspection of the enlarged opening initial and following letters corrected source capitalization Annua to ANnua; remaining opening letters and second-verse layout rechecked before resealing.

Fresh corpus source reading rechecked all 48 verses, every evidence note, headings, page furniture and full-page line starts. Supported source corrections: verse 46 forte to sorte. Prior independent second-pass history is retained; changed readings were additionally corroborated from native crops by /root/w_review_c. See W-3.10-second-pass.md.

lg.label: Elegia X. Ad Cererem, conquerens quod ejus sacris cum amicâ concumbere non permittatur.
lg.l: ANnua venerunt Cerealis tempora sacri.
Secubat in vacuo sola puella toro.
Flava Ceres, tenues spicis redimita capillos,
Cur inhibes sacris commoda nostra tuis?
Te, Dea, munificam gentes ubicumque loquuntur:
Nec minus humanis invidet ulla bonis.
Ante nec hirsuti torrebant farra coloni:
Nec notum terris area nomen erat.
Sed glandem quercus, oracula prima, ferebant,
Haec erat, & teneri cespitis herba, cibus.
Prima Ceres docuit turgescere semen in agris;
Falce coloratas subsecuitque comas.
Prima jugo tauros supponere colla coëgit;
Et veterem curvo dente revellit humum.
Hanc quisquam lacrimis laetari credit amantum,
Et bene tormentis secubituque coli?
Nec tamen est (quamvis agros amet illa feraces)
Rustica: nec viduum pectus amoris habet.
Cretes erunt testes; nec fingunt omnia Cretes:
Cretes, nutrito terra superba Jove.
Illic, sideream mundi qui temperat arcem,
Exiguus tenero lac bibit ore puer.
Magna fides testi: testis laudatur alumno.
Fassuram Cererem crimina nota puto.
Viderat Iäsium Cretaeâ Diva sub Idâ
Figentem certâ terga ferina manu.
Vidit, & ut tenerae flammam rapuere medullae;
Hinc pudor, ex aliâ parte trahebat amor.
Victus amore pudor. sulcos arere videres,
Et sata cum minimâ parte redire sui.
Cum bene jactati pulsarant arva ligones,
Ruperat & duram vomer aduncus humum,
Seminaque in latos iërant aequaliter agros;
Irrita decepti vota colentis erant.
Diva, potens frugum, silvis cessabat in altis:
Deciderant longae spicea serta comae.
Sola fuit Crete fecundo fertilis anno.
Omnia, quâ tulerat se Dea, messis erant.
Ipse locus nemorum canebat frugibus Ide,
Et ferus in silvâ farra metebat aper.
Optavit Minos similes sibi legifer annos:
Optavit Cereris longus ut esset amor.
Quod tibi secubitus tristes, Dea flava, fuissent;
Hoc cogor sacris nunc ego ferre tuis.
Cur ego sim tristis, cum sit tibi nata reperta;
Regnaque, quam Juno, sorte minora regat?
Festa dies, Veneremque vocat, cantusque merumque.
Haec decet ad dominos munera ferre Deos.
